questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Many of China's exports has been redirected to the domestic market in view of the more consumption-driven economy.

options.text: in view of the more consumption-driven economy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __***option 1***__ 

Many of China's exports is a plural subject so the verb should also be in its plural form.

Thus, we need to replace 'has been' with 'have been'.

**__Improved Sentence__:** *Many of China's exports **have been **redirected to the domestic market in view of the more consumption-driven economy.*

 [IMAGE: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/qDYrZqa9bQUqkqd199gfPANHfRcCyQkM8h-0ZOtd9QHwrvsslsR9F6G7cO89FghVbGAuk5TsJDbMr1huLuv0e6odFTtNj5qoJ5mVG8VYUqBROHSt-qg1DnTryx3wYvenUgTzua4W] **ADDITIONAL** **INFORMATION**-

**in view of** = because or as a result of.
Eg- "the poor condition of libraries is of concern in view of the increased emphasis on reference work"

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Two senior officers have been entrusted with the responsibility __by organize__ the reception of the guest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'of organizing'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

In the given sentence, the usage of **'by organize'** is incorrect Instead use **'of organizing' 

'Organize' is a verb **that means 'arrange systematically or in order.' 

__
 
• **In the given sentence,****'of'** is used which is a preposition and we know that we have to use **a prepositional object** after the preposition and it can be a **noun/pronoun.**
 
• **The prepositional object **can be a noun/pronoun/gerund, a Gerund is a verb form and if we make a gerund we have to use '**ing' **form after it.
 
• We have to use the preposition **'of' **instead of **'by'** because the former one means **'expressing the relationship between and general category and something which belongs to such category' **while** 'by' **means ‘**as a means of**’ something or someone.
 
• '**By**' preposition often comes in a **passive **sentence.
 
• From the meaning of preposition, we can say that the noun '**responsibility**' will take the preposition '**of**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When '**of**' is used after the noun '**responsibility'**, the definite article must be used before the noun.
 
• Let's see an example
 
 
• The governor-general has the** responsibility of** appointing the members of the Queen’s Privy Council for Canada.
 
 

**So the correct sentence is:** *Two senior officers have been entrusted with the responsibility **of organizing** the reception of the guest.*

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The merchant brought many gifts for his family from India.

options.text: Many gifts were brought by the merchant for his family from India.
His family were brought by the merchant for many gifts from India.
Many gifts brought by the merchant for his family from India.
Many gifts are brought by the merchant for his family from India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

Active => subject + v2 + object + other word.

Passive=> Object + was/were + v3 + by + subject + other words.

This structure is being followed by; only option 1.

So, the chose option is correct.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Bhola said to his friend, "How can I make this charcoal white?"

options.text: Bhola asked his friend how he could make that charcoal white.
Bhola told his friend how he could make that charcoal white.
Bhola asked his friend how can I make this charcoal white.
Bhola asked his friend how could he make that charcoal white.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• The given sentence is in interrogative form when changed into indirect form it becomes an assertive sentence.
 
• 'said to' changes to 'asked', first person changes to the third person, can changes to could, this changes to that.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sequence is followed by option 1 i.e.** '**Bhola asked his friend how he could make that charcoal white'.**

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

India's largest car-maker is evaluating the launch to a small electric car next year.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 4.**
 
• The error lies in the wrong usage of the preposition 'to' which is used to show direction.
 
• **The correct preposition to be used here is 'of' **which is used for belonging to, relating to, or connected with.
 
• In the above sentence, the launch is related to a small electric car.

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. But once when Mark disturbed the whole class with his pranks I had to reprimand him.

B. He was in third grade when I taught at Saint Mary's School.

C. All 34 students were dear to me, but Mark Eklund, was one in a million.

D. He had a happy-to-be-alive attitude that made even his occasional mischievousness delightful.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• Sentence C is talking about a person called 'Mark Eklund', sentence B is introducing that person.
 
• Sentence D is describing his personality and his mischievousness which is continued in sentence A that talks about one of his mischievous things.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sequence is followed in Option 1 i.e. CBDA.**

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. Once Oliver made a big snowman.

B. The fat snowman wore an old top hat and a muffler.

C. Now, it looked very grand indeed and Oliver's friends loved it.

D. It was as big as him but much fatter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ADBC.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The only independent sentence among the given sentences is A which is our first sentence.
 
• Sentence A is talking about Oliver making a big snowman which is continued in sentence D as it is describing how big the snowman is.
 
• **Therefore, option beginning with AD sequence is in Option 1 i.e. ADBC.**
